name: vhost Kernel Module Not Loaded (CVE-2026-74580)
description:
Ensures the vhost kernel module is not loaded (checked in /proc/modules). A local user can reconfigure a vring while a device IOTLB is attached and trigger out-of-bounds memory access in vhost, leading to information disclosure, data corruption or denial of service (CVE-2026-74580, CVSS 8.7). A driver compiled into the kernel is not detected. To mitigate, block autoloading with 'install vhost /bin/true' in /etc/modprobe.d/disable-vhost.conf and unload the vhost drivers.
Hosts running virtual machines: KVM/libvirt hypervisors use vhost for virtio networking, storage and vsock acceleration, so this rule is expected to fail there. Do not unload vhost while guests are running; removing it degrades guest I/O and guests that depend on vhost devices fail to start. On hypervisors, exclude the host from this rule or accept the finding, restrict local shell access to trusted administrators, and remediate by installing the patched kernel from the vendor errata and rebooting once available.
Required sudo rule (remedy only): allow user lea to run ONLY this exact command without a password: lea ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /sbin/modprobe -r vhost_net vhost_vsock vhost_scsi vhost

_remedy.command: modprobe -r vhost_net vhost_vsock vhost_scsi vhost 2>/dev/null; cat /proc/modules
